summary: Platform-specific package ships a WebRTC/WebSocket remote-control agent binary
details: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships a ~12MB linux/arm64 Go binary at bin/sxt whose linked modules include the full Pion WebRTC v4 stack (webrtc, ice, dtls, sctp, srtp, stun, turn, datachannel, interceptor), coder/websocket for signaling, and skip2/go-qrcode for pairing. This composition is the standard architecture of a remote-access agent: a remote peer signals via WebSocket, pairs via QR code, and opens a WebRTC data channel to the installer's host to send commands and receive responses. The package.json license field points to an unrelated personal repository (https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control) whose name and username do not match the package's `sextant` / `sxt` branding, and the tarball ships no README, source, or documentation explaining the binary. The name/description mismatch functions as a cover story around a remote-control payload targeting the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
